Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: Tanzania has general judicial oversight but no ID-specific mechanisms. Under RIPA, appeals for refusal or cancellation of ID go only to the Director of Registration and then the Minister (final decision) — courts cannot review ID refusals. The RIA 2021 report notes no independent judicial redress. General court system applies but no dedicated ID court oversight.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed via fetch of the original 2021 CIS/Research ICT Africa case study, which states RIPA appeals on ID refusal/cancellation go only to the Director then the Minister (whose decision is final), with no ID-specific judicial mechanism. Corroborated by a second, independent authoritative source: the Tanzania High Court's 2024 Magoti v Attorney-General judgment on the Personal Data Protection Act, which confirms Tanzanian courts retain general judicial review over administrative/'final' ministerial decisions (citing Tanzania Air Services v Minister for Labour) but that this oversight is general, not ID-specific. Value Code 2 (general oversight, not ID-specific) is well supported; single-source flag resolved, score confirmed unchanged.
